Discover and enquireStandard3–5 weeks

Admissions enquiries, counselor follow-up and campus tours

Enquiries from ads, the website, fairs, walk-ins and WhatsApp land in one CRM with their source, get an approved acknowledgment and a named counselor, and move to a campus tour or open-day slot with reminders and post-visit follow-up.

K-12 schools · Colleges & universities

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

In admission season, enquiries arrive faster than the front office can return calls. Leads sit in counselors' personal phones and spreadsheets, families who asked for a tour never get a slot, and the institution cannot tell which campaign or fair produced confirmed admissions.

Trigger

A parent or applicant submits a Meta or Google lead form or the website form, scans a fair or walk-in QR code, or messages the admissions WhatsApp number.

How it runs

  • Create or update one CRM record per family, de-duplicated by phone number, with source, campaign, grade or program, campus, and the consent and notice version shown on the form.
  • Send an approved WhatsApp acknowledgment with the prospectus link and the counselor's name, assigned by grade or program, campus and preferred language.
  • Answer common questions on fees, transport, dates and eligibility only from the approved prospectus and fee schedule; route anything else to the counselor with a short summary.
  • Offer campus tour and open-day slots from the admissions calendar, share directions and a visitor pass for the gate, and remind the family the day before with a one-tap reschedule.
  • After the visit, prompt the counselor to record the outcome and send the registration or application link the family asked for.
  • Escalate enquiries with no counselor contact within the agreed time to the admissions head, and report enquiries, tours and admissions by source each morning.

Human checkpoint

Counselors make every follow-up call and record outcomes, and the admissions head approves templates, answer content and assignment rules. The workflow never screens or ranks children or parents, and seats under RTE Section 12(1)(c) follow the state's own portal and process.

Visit, demo or trialStarter2–4 weeks

Demo class to enrollment for coaching institutes

Leads from ads, school seminars and walk-ins book a demo class, get reminders and, after attending, a counselor call informed by their demo feedback. The fee plan, installment schedule, refund policy and batch options go out in writing before any payment.

Coaching & test-prep institutes

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Coaching admissions peak around board results and entrance exam calendars. Demo attendees are not followed up consistently, counselors explain fees and refunds differently, and pressure tactics or rank promises in follow-up messages now attract consumer authority action.

Trigger

An aspirant or parent submits an ad or seminar form, walks in, or messages the institute about a course or demo class.

How it runs

  • Record the lead with course, target exam, class, center and source, and check the institute's minimum age and eligibility rules before offering a demo.
  • Offer demo slots by course and center, send an approved confirmation with timing and address, and remind the aspirant and, for minors, the parent before the class.
  • Mark demo attendance from the faculty's register or app, and send a two-question feedback form after the class.
  • Create a counselor task with the feedback and preferred batch timing; the counselor calls to discuss fit and preparation, never rank or selection promises.
  • Send the written fee plan, installment schedule, refund policy and batch options from approved templates, with a payment link only after the family confirms.
  • Report demo bookings, attendance and enrollments by course, center and source, and flag leads waiting more than a day for a call.

Human checkpoint

Counselors hold every enrollment conversation, and the center head approves any discount or installment change. The academic head and the institute's legal adviser approve all templates so that none promises selections, ranks or assured results.

Visit, demo or trialStandard4–6 weeks

Trial activation and paid conversion for online courses

Product events show which trial learners reached their first lesson, quiz or live session. Adult learners who opted in get nudges tied to their next step, under-18 accounts get service messages to the parent only, and the growth team sees conversion by course and channel.

EdTech & online learning

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Most trial sign-ups never finish a first lesson, and generic drip emails treat every learner the same. Behavior-based nudges suit adults but cannot be applied to children, and countdown pressure or hard-to-cancel trials are dark patterns under the consumer authority's guidelines.

Trigger

A learner starts a free trial or sample course on the website or app, or completes, skips or abandons a key activation step.

How it runs

  • Ask for age at sign-up and route under-18 learners to a parent consent step that checks the parent is an adult before the account is activated.
  • Track activation events such as first lesson, first quiz and first live session for adult accounts, and only the service events the course needs for child accounts.
  • Send adult learners who opted in an email or WhatsApp nudge tied to the step they have not reached, from approved templates with weekly caps.
  • For child accounts, send the parent only service messages such as the trial end date, the schedule and how to cancel.
  • Before the trial ends, show the price, renewal terms and a one-click cancel option, and send a reminder before any first charge.
  • Report activation and trial-to-paid conversion by course, cohort and channel, with child accounts excluded from every ad audience.

Human checkpoint

The growth lead approves every sequence, cap and template, and the data protection contact approves the age gate and parent consent flow. Refund and cancellation disputes go to the learner success lead, never to an automated reply.

Apply and enrollAdvanced5–7 weeks

Applications, document checklists and verification for colleges

Applicants complete one form with a program and category checklist. Uploads are checked for completeness, readability and name or date mismatches, the admissions office verifies each file in a queue, and missing items trigger reminders until the seat is confirmed.

Colleges & universities

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Applications arrive across counseling rounds with missing marksheets, blurred category certificates and names that differ between documents. Staff chase applicants by phone, originals are sometimes kept against the rules, and seats stay unconfirmed while the next round approaches.

Trigger

An applicant submits the online application, or the admissions office opens a counseling round and invites shortlisted applicants to complete their documents.

How it runs

  • Show the checklist for the chosen program and category, such as marksheets, entrance scorecard, transfer and migration certificates, and category or disability certificates.
  • Check each upload for type, readability and completeness, and extract name, date of birth and marks as a draft to compare across documents.
  • Place each file in the admissions office queue with mismatches and unreadable pages highlighted beside the original images.
  • Send polite reminders for missing or rejected items with the reason and deadline, and stop reminders once the file is complete.
  • Collect the anti-ragging undertaking reference number and the APAAR or ABC ID where applicable, and book an in-person slot to verify and return original certificates.
  • On approval, send the offer and fee link, write the confirmed student to the college ERP and update seat counts by program and category.

Human checkpoint

Admissions officers verify every document and decide eligibility, category and seat allocation; extraction only drafts. Originals are verified in person and returned at once, as UGC requires, and withdrawals and refunds follow the UGC fee refund policy with the registrar's approval.

Onboard and scheduleStandard3–5 weeks

Batch and cohort allocation with schedule change notices

New students are placed in batches or live cohorts by course, center or time zone, medium and timing within capacity. Faculty availability is checked, timetables are published, and every later change reaches only the affected students and parents.

Coaching & test-prep institutes · EdTech & online learning

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Batches fill unevenly, timing preferences live in spreadsheets, and schedule changes are announced in large groups that students mute. In coaching, timings may also need to respect school hours and daily limits under state coaching rules or the institute's own policy.

Trigger

A student completes enrollment, a batch reaches capacity, or a coordinator changes a class time, room, faculty member or mode.

How it runs

  • Read enrollments with course, center or time zone, medium and preferred timing, and propose placements within room and faculty capacity.
  • Check proposed timetables against the rules the institute sets, such as no classes during school hours, a weekly off and a maximum daily duration.
  • Show the plan to the academic coordinator, who adjusts and approves placements and timetables.
  • Publish each student's batch, timetable and room or joining link in the app, and confirm it to the student and, for minors, the parent.
  • When a class moves, notify only that batch with a one-tap acknowledgment, and re-send to anyone who has not opened it before the class.

Human checkpoint

The academic coordinator approves every placement, batch transfer and timetable change, and faculty confirm their availability. Requests to move a student between batches are decided by the academic head, never by the scheduler.

Attend and learnStandard3–5 weeks

Absence, late arrival and school bus alerts to parents

Students marked absent without approved leave trigger a private message to the parent by a set time, with reply buttons, and bus boarding, drop and delay updates come from RFID or attendant app events. Unresolved cases reach a staff member who calls the family.

K-12 schools · Coaching & test-prep institutes

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Calling every absent student's family takes a teacher's free period, so calls are late or skipped. Parents of bus students cannot tell whether their child boarded, and the transport office spends the morning answering the same calls.

Trigger

The attendance cutoff passes with a student marked absent and no approved leave, or a bus RFID reader or the attendant's app records a boarding, drop or delay.

How it runs

  • At the cutoff the institution sets, read attendance from the ERP or biometric system and list students absent without approved leave.
  • Send the parent an approved utility template with buttons for known reason, arriving late or did not know, and log the reply against the attendance record.
  • When the parent did not know or has not replied in the agreed time, alert the class teacher or coordinator on a dashboard so a staff member phones the family.
  • On RFID or attendant app events, notify the parent of boarding and drop, and send route delay notices only after the transport in-charge approves them.
  • If a child expected at a drop point is not marked off, alert the transport in-charge and the bus attendant at once to resolve by phone.
  • Show daily absences, late arrivals and unresolved cases, and give counselors a weekly list of repeated absences to follow up personally.

Human checkpoint

A named staff member phones every family that did not know about an absence, and the transport in-charge handles every missed drop or unusual delay by phone. Absence patterns are reviewed by the counselor or coordinator and never trigger automatic action.

Attend and learnStandard3–4 weeks

Circulars, homework digests and PTM booking for parents

Teachers post homework and circulars once in the ERP. Parents receive one daily digest per child in their chosen language, acknowledge consent slips with a tap, and book parent-teacher meeting slots from teachers' calendars.

K-12 schools

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Class WhatsApp groups mix homework, circulars and chatter, expose parents' numbers to each other and leave no record of who read a trip consent slip or a safety notice. PTM scheduling takes days of back-and-forth, and translated circulars depend on whoever has time.

Trigger

A teacher or coordinator publishes homework or a circular in the ERP, or the school opens a PTM window for a class.

How it runs

  • Collect the day's homework and approved circulars per class and assemble one digest per child at a time the school sets.
  • Draft translations into the languages parents chose, for a teacher fluent in that language to check before release.
  • Send the digest on WhatsApp to opted-in parents and through the parent app or email to the rest, with links to attachments instead of files in chat.
  • Track acknowledgments for circulars that need them, such as trip consent, and remind only the parents who have not responded.
  • For PTMs, offer slots from each teacher's availability, confirm with the room or video link, and send a reminder on the day.
  • Report delivery, acknowledgments and PTM attendance by class to the coordinator.

Human checkpoint

Class teachers approve their digests, a fluent teacher approves each translation, and the principal approves every school-wide circular and any message about safety, discipline or an incident. Parents' replies raising a concern go to the class teacher, not to an automated answer.

Attend and learnStandard3–4 weeks

Teacher absence and substitution planner

Leave recorded before a cutoff produces a proposed substitution plan from the timetable, matching free teachers by subject and sharing extra periods fairly. The vice-principal approves it, and substitutes get their periods and lesson notes before the first bell.

K-12 schools · Coaching & test-prep institutes

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Substitutions are worked out on paper before assembly by the one person who knows the timetable. The same willing teachers absorb most extra periods, lesson notes rarely reach the substitute, and in coaching an absent faculty member can leave a batch waiting with no class.

Trigger

A teacher records leave in the ERP or HR system, or submits a leave request through the staff form, before the daily cutoff.

How it runs

  • Read approved and pending leave for the day and list the periods or batch lectures that need cover.
  • Find teachers free in each period, preferring the same subject and class, and balance cover using each teacher's load for the week and term.
  • Show the proposed plan to the vice-principal or academic coordinator, with conflicts and unfilled periods highlighted.
  • On approval, notify each substitute with class, room and the absent teacher's lesson plan link, and update the display timetable.
  • In coaching, offer the coordinator a reschedule option for lectures that cannot be covered, and notify the batch once it is approved.
  • Report substitution load by teacher and term so leadership can see whether cover is shared fairly.

Human checkpoint

The vice-principal or academic coordinator approves every plan and can override any assignment. Leave approval stays with the principal or HR under the staff leave policy; the planner never approves or rejects leave.

Attend and learnStandard4–5 weeks

Student and learner helpdesk grounded in the handbook

Students, parents and online learners ask questions on WhatsApp, the portal or the app and get answers cited from the current handbook, fee policy, academic calendar or help center. Grievances, ragging reports and signs of distress go straight to people.

Colleges & universities · EdTech & online learning

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Department offices and support teams answer the same questions about exam forms, hostel rules, scholarships, certificates and refunds all term. Answers vary by who replies, and serious messages about harassment, ragging or distress can sit in the same inbox as routine queries.

Trigger

A student, parent or learner sends a question to the helpdesk WhatsApp number, the student portal or the in-app help widget.

How it runs

  • Screen every message first for ragging, harassment, self-harm or emergency words agreed with the owner; on a match, alert the named person at once and show the national anti-ragging helpline or Tele-MANAS, 14416.
  • Classify the rest into topics such as exams, fees, hostel, scholarships, certificates, login or refunds.
  • Answer only from the approved handbook, policy and help center documents, citing the section used; low-confidence answers are not sent.
  • Hand grievances to the institution's grievance channel, account-specific requests to the right office, and anything unanswered to a staffed queue with a summary.
  • Flag questions the documents could not answer so owners can update them, and re-index changed documents the same day.

Human checkpoint

The dean of students or learner success lead owns the sensitive-message rules and the staffed queue. Ragging reports go to the Anti-Ragging Committee and grievances to the Students' Grievance Redressal Committee; fee waivers, discipline and academic exceptions are decided only by the authorized office.

Attend and learnStandard3–5 weeks

Course progress nudges and cohort engagement

Learners who stall get a reminder tied to their next module or live session, cohorts get session and deadline reminders, and learners who stay inactive are flagged to a mentor instead of receiving more messages. Child accounts get parent-facing summaries only.

EdTech & online learning

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Completion falls after the first modules, live cohort attendance drops mid-course, and blanket reminder emails get ignored or unsubscribed. Mentors cannot tell which of hundreds of learners need a personal call, and learners under eighteen cannot be profiled for engagement nudges.

Trigger

A learner misses a planned module or assignment, a live session or deadline approaches, or an adult learner stays inactive for the period the team sets.

How it runs

  • Compute each adult learner's progress against the cohort plan from course platform events, and only completion status for child accounts.
  • Send live session and assignment deadline reminders on the channel each learner chose, with a weekly message cap.
  • For adults who stall, send one nudge tied to the next module, with a link back to where they left off.
  • After repeated inactivity, stop automated nudges and create a mentor task with the learner's progress summary.
  • Send parents of under-18 learners a weekly progress summary and session schedule, with no behavior-based targeting.
  • Report completion, attendance and mentor outreach by cohort and course.

Human checkpoint

Mentors decide whom to call and what support to offer, and the learning lead approves caps and wording. Extensions, deferrals and refunds are decided by the learner success lead under the published policy.

Assess and reportAdvanced5–7 weeks

Test analytics and doubt routing to faculty

Each mock test produces a private topic and time analysis against the student's own history for the student, parent and mentor. Doubts sent as photos or text are tagged by subject and chapter and queued to the right faculty, with similar solved questions attached.

Coaching & test-prep institutes · EdTech & online learning

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Test results show marks and ranks but not which topics or habits cost marks. Doubts sent by photo in crowded groups wait days or reach the wrong teacher, and mentors notice a struggling student only after several poor tests.

Trigger

Results of a mock or practice test are published from the test platform or OMR scanner, or a student submits a doubt in the app, portal or doubt WhatsApp number.

How it runs

  • Import question-level responses and compute accuracy and time by subject, chapter and difficulty, compared with the student's previous tests.
  • Publish a private analysis to the student and, for minors, the parent, with practice sets from the institute's own question bank and no public rank lists.
  • Alert the student's mentor when scores drop sharply or tests are missed, with the analysis attached for a conversation.
  • Read submitted doubt photos or text, tag subject, chapter and question type, and attach similar solved questions from the institute's bank.
  • Queue each doubt to the right faculty or doubt solver with a response target; faculty may start from an AI-drafted hint that they edit before sending.
  • Report doubt volume, resolution time and recurring weak topics to the academic head for remedial classes.

Human checkpoint

Faculty answer every doubt and approve any drafted hint before it reaches a student. Mentors decide on counseling or extra classes, and any sign of stress or distress goes to the institute's counselor, never to an automated message.

Assess and reportStandard3–4 weeks

Report cards and results released securely to families

Once the principal or examination controller locks results, each report card or grade card is generated and the parent or adult student is notified with a secure, expiring link. PTM booking or revaluation options follow in the same notice.

K-12 schools · Colleges & universities

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Report cards are printed, signed and handed out on one crowded day, or forwarded as PDFs in groups where they can reach the wrong family. Corrections after release are messy, and colleges field calls about grade cards, revaluation windows and supplementary exams.

Trigger

The principal or examination controller marks results as final in the ERP or examination system for a class, program or semester.

How it runs

  • Generate each student's report or grade card from the locked results using the approved template and the remarks teachers entered.
  • Check for missing marks, unapproved remarks or records the exam office has flagged, and hold those until the exam office clears them.
  • Notify the parent or adult student with an approved template and a secure link that opens after a one-time code, never the document in chat.
  • Include the PTM booking link for schools, or revaluation and supplementary exam windows and fees for colleges.
  • Log every open, resend on request, and point families to DigiLocker where the board or university issues documents through it.

Human checkpoint

The principal or examination controller locks results and approves release, and teachers own their remarks. Revaluation, grace marks and any hold on a result are decided only by the examination office under the institution's rules, never by the workflow.

Tools

Respectful fee reminders, payment links and receipts

Fee payers receive courteous reminders before and after due dates with a UPI payment link, receipts arrive instantly, and installment, concession or refund requests go to the accounts office. Reminders never reach children, class groups or noticeboards.

K-12 schools · Colleges & universities · Coaching & test-prep institutes

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Accounts staff chase dues by phone, reminders sometimes reach the wrong parent or a class group, and children can be embarrassed when dues are raised in class. Installment and refund requests get lost between the front office and accounts, and receipts are issued by hand.

Trigger

A fee installment approaches or passes its due date in the ERP fee ledger, a payment succeeds or fails at the gateway, or a fee payer asks about fees.

How it runs

  • Read due dates, amounts and concessions from the ERP fee ledger and send an approved reminder to the registered fee payer a set number of days before the due date.
  • Include a payment link for UPI, cards and net banking, and post successful payments to the ledger with an instant receipt, or a GST invoice where the fee is taxable.
  • After the due date, send no more than the agreed number of courteous reminders, each with an option to request an installment plan or speak to accounts.
  • Route installment, concession, scholarship and refund requests to the accounts officer with the student's ledger summary and the applicable refund policy.
  • Give accounts a daily view of dues, promises to pay and failed payments, with no list shared with teachers or classes.

Human checkpoint

The accounts officer decides installment plans, concessions and refunds, and the principal or registrar approves reminder wording and frequency. Any step that affects a student's classes, exams or results is a management decision under the institution's policy and the law, never automated.

Uses fee payer contact, student name, class and amounts due, sent only to the registered fee payer. Messages state amounts and links, never compare students or threaten consequences. Payment records follow accounting retention rules, and reminder logs are kept for the academic year.

  • Payment links and automatic receipts
  • Accounts request queue

  • Installment requests resolved within the agreed time
  • Refunds paid within the published timeline

Alumni directory, events and mentoring

Graduating students opt in to the alumni network, profiles are refreshed by a short annual form, event invitations go to relevant batches and cities, and mentor matches between alumni and current students are approved by the alumni office.

Colleges & universities

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Alumni records go stale within a few years of graduation, invitations go to dead email addresses, and mentoring and placement referrals depend on a few personal networks. Reunions and giving drives are organized from scratch each time.

Trigger

A student graduates and is invited to join, an annual profile refresh falls due, or the alumni office schedules an event, mentoring round or giving campaign.

How it runs

  • Invite graduating students to opt in with a consent screen that states how their details will be used and what other alumni can see.
  • Send an annual refresh form for employer, city and mentoring interests, and mark records that bounce or stay unconfirmed.
  • Segment invitations by batch, program and city, and track registrations and attendance for each event.
  • Suggest mentor matches between opted-in alumni and current students by field and interest, for the alumni office to approve and introduce.
  • Report profile freshness, event attendance and mentoring activity, and acknowledge every gift with a receipt from the accounts office.

Human checkpoint

The alumni relations officer approves every campaign, introduction and mentor match, and current students choose whether to accept a mentor. Directory details are shown to other alumni only where each person chose to share them.

What we deliver

  • Annual refresh and event campaigns
  • Mentor matching workflow
  • Alumni engagement dashboard

  • Event registration and attendance
